cites.quote: API tests use Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with a fixed clock.

Web tests use
Vitest with jsdom and Testing Library.
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID
Without either, database tests are skipped.
The verifier skips coverage (the project has no coverage script), so no run reports coverage.
adds `visit_summary` to the existing patient response
AC3: Given any patient, when staff open the patient page, then every section other than the new Visit summary is shown as before.
The top-level response keys are not asserted.

findings.suggested_fix: Optionally assert the full top-level key set of GET /api/patients/:id, and render at least one appointment in the web fixture to show the list still appears below the summary.
findings.text: S-3 AC3 (every section other than Visit summary is shown as before) is only partly tested. The API checks medical history and the visit_summary keys but not the other top-level fields. The web fixture has appointments: [], so the list is never rendered. The artifact discloses this.

rubric_items.reason: Tests cover the repo count, the service field on GET, the 404 path, PATCH ignoring the field and the page block. Attempt-1 gaps are fixed: S-2 AC5 is tested in both layers, REQ-7 checks exact order and REQ-9 uses dates four weeks apart.

Assertions check exact count objects, the exact startsAt order, the rendered dt/dd values and the PATCH status, applied address and unchanged counts. The weak 'not.toEqual' isolation check is now exact per-patient counts.
Covers all three zero edges (none, Completed-only, No-show-only), closed appointments far apart with the clock moved, unknown patient 404, and visit_summary sent in a PATCH alongside a real edit.

API tests use Vitest and Supertest with a fresh database, a fixed injectable clock and describe.skipIf(!pgAvailable()). Web tests use Vitest, jsdom and Testing Library in web/src/__tests__. Every name starts with HMS-5 and its REQ id.
The artifact states no pass counts or coverage and defers to the verifier (H3). The verifier log shows 11 and 5 tests passing, which matches the artifact. The coverage step was skipped (exit 78).
